stories.title: Agility Robotics begins trading on Nasdaq after SPAC merger
paragraphs: The Robot Report says Agility Robotics began trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 5, 2026, under the ticker AGLT after completing its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI. Shares opened at $11.26, above the $10 SPAC deal price, and were at $10.30 as of the article's press time.

According to the report, Churchill XI shareholders approved the deal on Nov. 2 with more than 84% of votes cast in favor, and the transaction closed Nov. 4. Gross proceeds were about $465 million before expenses, including roughly $164 million from the trust after redemptions, $201 million from a Foxconn-led PIPE, and a $100 million funding round closed after the SPAC announcement.

Agility says Digit has logged more than 65,000 operating hours across nine customer facilities, including AGCO, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Mercado Libre, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada. The company reported $1.78 million in 2025 revenue and more than $300 million in committed multiyear orders for next-generation Digit 5, with early-access deliveries expected in 2027. CEO Peggy Johnson called the listing a way to accelerate putting robots into more workplaces.

stories.title: Boston Dynamics unveils Stretch Gen 2 for faster trailer unloading and repairs
paragraphs: Boston Dynamics announced Stretch Gen 2 on Nov. 3, 2026, as the next generation of its autonomous mobile trailer-unloading robot. RoboticsTomorrow reports the redesign draws on more than 100,000 operating hours and tens of millions of boxes unloaded by first-generation Stretch to cut unplanned downtime.

According to the company release carried by RoboticsTomorrow, Gen 2 uses automotive-grade connectors, an upgraded gripper with finer sensing, continuous-rotation joints that no longer hit hard stops, and about 81% less internal cabling—removing a major source of electrical faults. Exterior panels and a recessed emergency stop are meant to reduce accidental stoppages from falling boxes.

Boston Dynamics says a full swerve-drive swap now takes about one hour instead of a full day, and onboard diagnostics aim to let customer teams handle more routine service. Stretch Gen 2 can unload up to 1,000 cases per hour depending on case weight and stacking, runs about two shifts per charge, and fast-charges to 90% in about 75 minutes.

stories.title: Robot moth grows a new UV sensor from chemicals in its artificial blood
paragraphs: New Atlas reports that engineers at the University of Tartu and the Italian Institute of Technology built a moth-shaped robot that forms a new ultraviolet sensor in its 3D-printed body when ultraviolet light triggers chemicals in about 3 ml of artificial blood circulating through tiny veins.

According to first author Kadri-Ann Pankratov, pyrrole in the fluid turns into conductive polypyrrole where UV hits a stenciled wing patch, and gold wires printed into the body read the resistance drop so the robot can blink an LED or flap its wings. The sensor still worked after four months in storage.

New Atlas notes the prototype cannot fly, uses an external power supply for nitinol wing actuators, and relies on researchers—not the robot—to decide when and where to grow the sensor. The study appears in Advanced Science; the team says future circulatory systems might flush and reuse different chemistries.

image.credit: Kadri-Ann Pankratov et al., via New Atlas
